items.historicalDataImpact: ASSESSED 2026-09-10 by tracing origin/master; NOT measured against production data. Production CAN auto-post a wrong receipt total and credit the bank short. Verified chain on master: (1) capture routes a PDF through `ocrService.extractFromPdf`, which tries the VLM first and falls back to the regex `extractFromText` when the VLM is unavailable, returns nothing, or throws, and the PDF has text (ocrService.ts:52-75). Image receipts are VLM-only and are NOT exposed. (2) the regex `extractAmounts` takes the first matching pattern at its LEFTMOST occurrence (ocrExtractionService.ts:161-162), so a multi-section receipt can yield an intermediate section total. (3) `computeConfidence` (ocrExtractionService.ts:237) scores up to 1.00 and awards +0.25 for ANY total > 0 — it rewards the presence of a total, not its correctness; a receipt with vendor+date+total+VAT+lines scores 0.85. (4) there are TWO unattended auto-post paths on master, neither of which consults extraction warnings: `capture/[id]/post-expense.ts:243` (`shouldAutoPostReceipt(total, confidence, {maxAmount: 5000, minConfidence: 0.80})`) and `receipt-to-journal.ts:88` (same gate at minConfidence 0.85). EXPOSED POPULATION: PDF receipts under R5 000, auto-posted, on occasions the VLM failed or was unavailable. UNKNOWN and needs Hein: how often the VLM fails in production, and therefore how many such receipts exist. CREDIT NOTES — VERIFIED 2026-09-10: `detectDocumentType` classifies them as `credit_note` (ocrExtractionService.ts:24), but NEITHER auto-post path consults `documentType` — confirmed by the absence of any `documentType`/`credit_note` reference in post-expense.ts, receipt-to-journal.ts and receiptToJournalService.ts on master. So a credit note printed with positive figures (`Total - 115.00`, `115.00-`, `-R115.00`) auto-posts as a PURCHASE — EXP 100 / VAT 15 / bank CREDIT 115 — reversing the direction of the posting. The '+115 read' half is the K-072 r8 reviewer's measurement; the 'nothing consults the type' half is verified here. Do not query production from an agent; impact SQL belongs in fix.md.

items.claim: Portal token and payment-link routes use the default companyThe routes read the user's default company rather than the active one, minting tokens against the wrong tenant.
items.correctedTrigger: Three authenticated portal actions (generate.ts, [token].ts handleGenerateToken, payment-link.ts POST) re-derived the company from company_users ORDER BY is_default instead of withAuth's active company. A multi-company user whose active company is not the default got 404 for the active company's invoice and no token or link was written. customer_invoices RLS USING admits every member company (only WITH CHECK is the active one), so an invoice in the default company was read: an existing token was returned for the non-active company, otherwise the write failed WITH CHECK and 500'd. Not an outsider leak: the user belongs to both.
items.severityRationale: Corrected from high to medium: a functional 404 for multi-company users, not a tenant-boundary break. The only cross-company read is to a member of that company; no wrong row was written.

items.title: Approvals are not enforced anywhere: checkApproval and requestApproval have no caller, so any document posts under an active owner-only rule with no approval ever requested
items.source: Raised by the K-043 fixer while closing review-k043-r3 M2; recorded 2026-09-09
items.processNotes: Confirmed by the K-043 r4 blind reviewer, who grepped every caller: checkApproval and requestApproval have NO caller at all -- not in the five posting services, not in the UI. K-043 enforces WHO may decide an approval that exists; nothing creates one and nothing blocks posting without one. Today an operator can post any invoice, bill, payment, journal or credit note of any amount under an active owner-only rule with no approval request ever existing, i.e. the approvals feature is decorative in production and any control relying on it is not operating. The reviewer ruled deferring this out of K-043 defensible -- it spans five posting services and needs a document-level approval_status -- but it must not be left implicit. K-043's module doc and fix.md are being corrected to say only the DECIDE path is enforced. HEIN: if approvals are being represented to anyone as a control, that representation is currently false. 2026-09-26: PR1 of the enforcement series (#540, infra, nothing enforced yet: digest binding, per-company/per-type opt-in enforcement table, gate module, sole-approver rule per Hein Q2, requester re-stamp + past-requester refusal). Hein's decisions: enforce path by path starting with supplier invoices; opt-in default off; imports exempt; payments = instructions only; journals = manual only. PR2 must: refuse the content's last editor; gate honours only approvals decided >= enabled_at; settle past-requester UX. Deploy step: browser-approve one supplier-invoice request on dev after 708. Before enabling anywhere Hein runs the census in the R-035 design (active rules per company). 2026-09-27: PR1 (#540, merged 36eed4aab) deployed at 3edfa5c5d — infrastructure only, nothing enforced; merge round aligned disable-enforcement with R-048's ladder (shared mayWeakenAtLevel) and composed with R-032's guard. items.title: An admin can lower an admin-level approval rule to manager and re-raise the request, so a manager approves what only an admin should
items.source: Found by the K-043 r7 blind reviewer, outside the scope of the required_role ratchet; recorded 2026-09-10
items.processNotes:
K-043's migration-669 ratchet (snapshot required_role at raise, rebind may only RAISE it, assertMayDecide demands max(snapshot, live)) held against every lever the reviewer could drive -- except this one, which sits OUTSIDE it. An admin edits an ADMIN-level rule down to manager and then re-raises the request; the new request snapshots the already-lowered role, so the ratchet has nothing higher to hold to. Reproduced end to end: manager approves, 200. The ratchet is the right mechanism and should not be changed for this; the missing control is that lowering a rule's authority is itself a privileged act that an actor at that rank should not be able to perform on their own governing rule. Needs its own item and its own design. Related: R-032 (admin impersonation), R-033 (sole-owner deadlock), R-035 (no enforcement path at all).

The inventory is in docs/audits/remediation/K-107/fix.md. Headlines: (1) confirmCustomerPayment / cancelCustomerPayment are the unfixed AR twins of the supplier-payment defect -- HIGH, they post to the ledger. (2) approveVATAdjustment is byte-for-byte the adjustment shape already fixed -- HIGH. (3) generateJournalFromRecurring lacks company_id on its UPDATE -- a multi-tenant violation. (4) The DB triggers trg_cp_payment_number and trg_sp_payment_number mint MAX+1 with NO UNIQUE INDEX on either payments table -- the same shape as the stock-adjustment defect, on the two tables that carry money. items.severityRationale: Every guard this programme added is unenforced on the path code actually merges through.
items.historicalDataImpact: Any PR merged green on GitHub was never checked by eleven of the sixteen gates.
items.title: Eleven of the sixteen CI gates never run on GitHub, so a PR can be green while the repo's own guards fail
items.source: Found while investigating why K-015's local CI failed on a PR GitHub reported green; recorded 2026-09-10
items.processNotes: scripts/ci/run-ci.sh defines 16 gates. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs only FIVE of them: agent-docs, type-check, lint, user-id-casts, unit-tests (plus the separate Golden Paths job). NEVER run on GitHub: security-guards, is-active-filters, raw-transactions, vat-guard-coverage, self-defining-universe, findings-numbering, migration-rls, component-tests, migration-naming, integration-tests, build. Several of those are financial-integrity guards this very programme wrote -- is-active-filters, vat-guard-coverage, migration-rls, migration-naming. They fire only when a human or agent runs `bun run ci` locally. PROVEN, not theorised: K-015 at 57779e48d fails `is-active-filters` locally (a balance query filtering is_active, which would hide a real opening-balance residual) while GitHub reports 'Type Check, Lint & Test: SUCCESS' and 'Golden Paths E2E: SUCCESS' and the PR shows mergeStateStatus CLEAN. Only the branch being a DRAFT stopped it being mergeable. This is the same family as R-041 (migration warnings printed into a void): a guard exists, is believed to be running, and is not. It also explains how defects of the audited classes reached master in the first place. HEIN: the cheap fix is to make the GitHub job run `bun run ci` (or the gate subset that does not need a database) rather than five hand-listed steps that drift from run-ci.sh every time a gate is added. 2026-09-25: re-proved with canary PR #521 (is-active-filters violation; GitHub green, mergeStateStatus CLEAN). On 0ecf6d06e run-ci.sh has 17 gates and GitHub ran 5. Fixed: the quality job runs `bun run ci`; new gate workflow-runs-ci (YAML-parsed exact allow-list of triggers, job keys, the 3 steps, gate env and package.json scripts.ci) refuses every bypass found in blind review. MAIN RESIDUAL, Hein's call: no required status checks exist (branch protection API 403 on this plan), so a red check does not block merge -- #496 merged with Type Check FAILED. Also: integration tests still skip on GitHub (empty DATABASE_URL secret). 2026-09-26: merged as b6e9d70e7 (CI-only; effective on GitHub from the merge, no prod runtime change). Final-head GitHub run 36131157091: quality pass (all 18 non-skipped gates), Golden Paths pass. Residual 1 decided by Hein 2026-09-26: merge convention (gh pr checks all-pass on the exact head, then --match-head-commit) recorded in CLAUDE.md.

items.processNotes:
`SUM(ABS(gjl.credit - gjl.debit))` applies ABS to each LINE before summing, so a contra line adds instead of subtracting. Correct is `ABS(SUM(...))` or a plain signed SUM. Confirmed present on origin/master at notes16to20.ts:125,163,173 and notes26to30.ts:82,85 -- i.e. deployed, not branch-introduced. Measured on the fixture: R100,000 sales less an R8,000 credit note prints R108,000 in note 18 while the income statement says R92,000; note 19 prints R4,000 vs R2,000; note 27 prints a 'profit of R 9 000,00' where net profit is R19,000. `bun run ci` passes all 15 gates at exit 0 because integration-tests self-skips without DATABASE_URL, so the gate cannot catch it. items.source: Noted by the R-058 fixer; confirmed on origin/master by the orchestrating session — the UPDATE carries no status predicate.
items.processNotes:
`captureRouterService.routeEvent` runs `UPDATE capture_events SET status = 'extracting', updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1 AND company_id = $2` — no `AND status <> 'posted'`. The documented flow is received → extracting → extracted | failed, so 'posted' is outside it and should be refused. Fix: predicate the UPDATE and refuse when it matches no row. R-058's reviewer has been asked to judge whether this belongs inside R-058, since it defeats that branch's own guard.

SEVERITY CORRECTED 2026-09-10 from high to medium, on the R-058 reviewer's measurement — I had registered it without testing reachability. It also measured what happens IF reached, by applying routeEvent's exact statement to a posted event and re-posting through the real handlers:
  - post.ts: re-post 409 — stopped by the duplicate-fingerprint gate, NOT by the guard.
  - post-expense (GL path): re-post 500 — stopped by `uq_gl_je_capture_source_document`, NOT by the guard.
  - post-expense (employee expense claim): re-post **200, claims 1 → 2 — a DOUBLE POST with no backstop**; `expense_claim_lines` carries only the non-unique `idx_expense_lines_source_doc`.
So both the 'already posted' refusal and R-058's FOR UPDATE lock see a non-posted row and let it through. Two of the three paths are saved by constraints unrelated to this guard. Fix the predicate anyway — the protection is an accident of the call graph, and the expense-claim path has nothing behind it.

RECOMMENDED BACKSTOP (2026-09-10, R-058 reviewer): give `expense_claim_lines` a partial-unique index on its source document, as `gl_journal_entries` already has (`uq_gl_je_capture_source_document`). The employee expense-claim path is the only capture path with NO constraint behind its guard — measured: a re-post there creates a second claim where the other two paths are stopped by a unique index or a fingerprint gate. A database constraint also protects routes that have no guard at all (R-070). Not built in R-058 round 2 — it needs a migration and was not one of that round's scored findings. Pre-flight: count existing duplicate source documents in expense_claim_lines before creating the index, since it will refuse to build over them.

items.severityRationale: MEASURED 2026-09-10 on origin/master e86b10664 (isaflow_dev, probe-r075): all three outcomes occur, depending on pool state. (a) Under load the pool hands the released client to the next request, so routeEvent's post-VLM writes run INSIDE that request's transaction as app_user with its claims: with a different user, RLS matches 0 rows, 'extraction complete' is logged and the event is stuck in 'extracting' forever; with the same user acting as company B, captured_documents fails WITH CHECK and B's request 500s with its own writes rolled back (cross-tenant interference); an extraction-error 'failed' write commits or rolls back with B. (b) Pool idle: autocommit as postgres (superuser, bypasses RLS); the 'extracting' UPDATE escapes like this on EVERY run. (c) Idle past 30s: the client is closed and the event is stuck in 'extracting'. No foreign-tenant data leaked (every statement filters company_id = A). Reachable through the cookie-session upload path only; inbound-email and the API-key upload path have no ALS store.

items.processNotes:
Same class as K-226 (fire-and-forget on the request transaction), at a different site. Fix direction: run background work outside the request's ALS context (als.exit / a fresh context with its own pooled connection and its own company GUCs), or enqueue it. First step for the fixer: MEASURE which of the outcomes above actually occurs.

Fix constraint (measured): routeEvent is started BEFORE the request COMMITs, so wrapping it in als.exit alone never sees the uncommitted event. It must run after commit: an after-commit queue drained outside the request context, or a worker claiming status='received'. Also make neon.ts refuse a released client. K-226 is the same family, a different mechanism (already awaited and savepointed on master). Report: scratchpad probe-r075.md.

items.severityRationale: A user who corrects an auto-posted entry with a manual offsetting journal instead of a reversal gets that correction applied twice when the run is undone. The money is wrong on the ledger and the run still reads undone. Needs a design decision, not a patch: a hand offset carries no reversal_of_id and no reversed_at, so it is indistinguishable from any other credit, and a heuristic that treats matching credits as reversals would refuse legitimate undos.

Cause: the IS and BS business-unit tests fired `change` on the BU <select> as soon as the 'All Business Units' placeholder rendered, before the business-units fetch added the 'business-a' option. happy-dom then left the value '', so no BU was selected and the waitFor on the report URL (:89, :133) timed out. No separate timeout gap was found; every failure had this one signature. Review round 1 MEDIUM: the same defect in CostCentreComparatorGate. Also: deriveSageVat with STATED figures can return taxAmount = total - subtotal < 0, which migration 692's leg arms now refuse — so reviving this importer means handling that branch, not just the SELECT. Both Sage importers guard the TOTAL only (AR `< 0`, AP `> 0`), never the legs, so a stated-figure row whose derived tax is negative reaches migration 692's tax-leg arm and fails per-row with the raw trigger message instead of a named one. The next Sage import round should add the leg check beside the total check. 2026-09-24: fixed on fix/r101-sage-ar-import-20260924 — migration 694 adds gl_customer_invoice_id; negative staged total -> migration_status 'credit_note'; the leg concern is moot (no staging table states VAT; statedSageFigures removed). 2026-09-24: merged (PR #489, 447b5b2d7) and deployed 07:07 SAST; migration 694 applied on prod.

items.severityRationale: Customer-facing wrong balance, three causes. Per cause, from r095-measure-screens.log: (1) receipt rule 900 vs 500 (1000 received, 600 allocated); (2) 'approved'-only credit notes 900 vs 450; (3) default window -400 vs 600. Combined case: Measured 1534.56 against a correct 1134.56: +200 from the receipt rule (300 received, 100 allocated, same defect as R-112) and +200 from dropping an 'applied' credit note (status = 'approved' only; the email counts approved, partially_applied and applied, an applied note at applied_amount — the email's rule is right). The window did not contribute there (all activity inside a year). The window ALONE misstates older activity: invoice 1000 dated 400 days ago plus a receipt of 400 last month shows -400 (in credit) against a true 600 by default; 600 with fromDate covering the full history.

items.claim: Several writers accept a NEGATIVE total_amount onto customer_invoices/supplier_invoices, and no CHECK constraint or trigger forbids it (verified on the schema fixture). Confirmed unguarded: recurring-template EXECUTION (core/recurringTemplateLines.ts headerTotals/normaliseLines — templateData is opaque JSON from the request body, and the create-time qty/price guard does not re-run), the AI capture pipeline (pages/api/accounting/ai-invoice-pipeline.ts and capture/[id]/post.ts — validatePipelineInput checks null/undefined only), time-entry billing (pages/api/accounting/time-entries-invoice.ts, and createTimeEntry does not guard hours/rate), and the Sage AR import (core/sageCustomerImportService.ts skips totalAmount === 0 but not < 0, unlike its AP sibling). A negative-total document is an ad-hoc credit note outside credit_notes: it is invisible to the ageing and the subledger (both filter balance > 0) while its journal, if posted, stands in the GL.

2026-09-27: Seen on the R-035 PR2 push. Not diagnosed: likely a timing-sensitive waitFor. Reproduce under load before fixing.

2026-09-28: NOT REPRODUCED on origin/master 7d992b3e5; stays candidate. 62 executions, 0 failures: 20 sequential runs of the file under added CPU load (busy loops, loadavg 23->38); 20 runs as 4 rounds of 5 concurrent vitest processes (load ~18); 2 full component-suite runs (bun run test:components, 738/738 each) at load 22->32; 20 sequential runs at load 25-28. Code read: none of the page's non-mocked children fires an extra apiFetch that could consume a queued mockResolvedValueOnce, and the post-PUT setState calls batch together, so no logic race was found. The original failure output was not recoverable from the R-035 PR2 session. Not fixed: the only candidate mechanism left is testing-library's 1000 ms default findBy/waitFor timeout under extreme contention, and lengthening a timeout without a reproduction is not a fix. Reopen with the failing output if it recurs. Related: R-138 (ReportPageDrillDimensions timeout under load, seen again 2026-09-28 in an R-148 CI run).

2026-09-28 (later): REPRODUCED by starving only the test process: `taskset -c <1 core> bunx vitest run --config vitest.components.config.ts --maxWorkers=12` with the target plus the 11 heaviest component files gave 4/72 failures on master, all 'Unable to find an element with the text: Edit' at :83 in 'closes the form and refetches when the save succeeds', with the button reading 'Saving...' in the DOM dump. Full suite pinned to 1-2 cores: 0/10; the target alone on 1 core passes. Cause: not a timeout (the failing test ran in ~155 ms). waitFor(queryByText('Save') === null) is satisfied mid-save, because the button is relabelled 'Saving...' and the batched setEditing(false)/setIsLoading(true) commit shows the spinner, so the synchronous getByText('Edit') raced the PUT and the refetch. Fix (test-only, #562): await findByText('Edit'), which can only resolve on the atomic final commit, then assert that the refetched notes render and 'Save' is gone. Same pinning on the branch: 0/72. No timeout changed. Mutations: the page swallowing the refusal, the form never closing, and the refetch removed each turn a named test red; master's test passed the refetch-removed mutant. The recipe is in tests/unit/components/.claude.md. Blind review: SHIP, no findings.

items.claim: notifyAnnotationReceived JOINs users to find the company's owners/admins/managers. It is called from a withPortalAuth route that sets no request.jwt.claims, so if the connection is subject to users_self_read (FORCE RLS, id = auth.uid()), auth.uid() is NULL and no recipient resolves.

On isaflow_dev the raw pool connects as postgres with rolbypassrls = true, so users_self_read does not apply on this path there and recipients should resolve. Prod's pool role (from /home/velo/isaflow/.env.local) was NOT checked. Close only after confirming prod's connecting role, or with an integration test that forces app_user plus RLS on this path.

2026-09-28 (later): FALSE POSITIVE, disconfirmed on prod with a read-only catalog query (Hein OK): the prod pool (/home/velo/isaflow/.env.local DATABASE_URL, database isaflow) connects as postgres with rolbypassrls = true. users and company_users have FORCE RLS, but a BYPASSRLS role is exempt from it. pages/api/accounting/portal/documents/[documentId]/annotate.ts is wrapped only by withPortalAuth, which sets no ALS client, so notifyAnnotationReceived runs on the raw pool (src/lib/neon.ts uses the ALS client only when withAuth set one, and only that client does SET LOCAL ROLE app_user). users_self_read therefore never applies on this path, and recipients resolve on both dev and prod. The residual risk, recorded rather than fixed: if the pool role ever loses BYPASSRLS, this and every other raw-pool read of users breaks silently.

items.title: A route whose auth wrapper buffers res.end hangs the client when the handler throws, unless withErrorHandler sits inside the wrapper
items.claim: withAuth (and bearerPipeline, withExtensionToken) replace res.end with a buffer and replay it only when the handler returns normally; on a throw they ROLLBACK and rethrow without replaying, so any 500 written after that (by an outer withErrorHandler or by Next) never reaches the client and the request hangs until the socket times out. Known instance: pages/api/invitations/revoke/[id].ts is withAuth(withCsrf(handler)) with no withErrorHandler. payment-link POST had it and was fixed under R-157. Routes behind bearerPipeline / withExtensionToken were not censused.
items.processNotes: 2026-09-29: Reported by the blind reviewers of PR #567 (R-157 round 4: executed for payment-link, reasoned for invitations/revoke). Not fixed. Options: add withErrorHandler inside the wrapper on each such route, or have the wrappers replay a 500 on a throw (one fix for every route). Census first: every export wrapping withAuth / withBearerOrCookieAuth / withExtensionToken without an inner withErrorHandler. 2026-09-30: Census (AST, every pages/api route): 640 of 642 compose withErrorHandler inside the wrapper; invitations/revoke/[id] has none; capture/upload has both an outer and an inner one. No route relies on the rethrow. Fixed in the wrappers (Hein's choice): on a throw each rolls back, restores the real res.end and answers with withErrorHandler's responder; no rethrow (confirmed by Hein 2026-09-30). RED 17/22 on origin/master (R-159/red.int.log). Review round 1 (general SHIP, 3 LOW) and round 2 (adversarial FIX, 2 MEDIUM + 4 LOW, all latent) fixed: replayEnd keeps a post-COMMIT replay failure out of the catch; withErrorHandler marks a flushed failure 500 and aborts it; flushed failures abort instead of completing; answerThrow restores end first and survives unreadable errors. Mutants: 56/56 RED on the round-2 code. Round 3 (both SHIP): withErrorHandler's flushed-failure mark+abort limited to responses not yet ended. /review (fresh blind agent, APPROVED, 6 LOW) fixed: accurate throw log with the ROLLBACK outcome, ended responses never aborted by answerThrow, pre-swap throw integration case; the census stays fail-closed on any .end assignment (a receiver filter missed apiRes.end). Rounds 4-5: census also catches Object.defineProperty/defineProperties/assign (incl. computed key) and Reflect.set of end, with fixture cases; a key held in a variable is the named limit. Mutants: 71/71 RED. Follow-up noted: evict a connection whose ROLLBACK failed (client.release(true)). Merged as #577 (ca5f32867). 2026-09-30: merged and deployed to prod ca5f32867 at 11:24 SAST on Hein's explicit business-hours 'Deploy now' (the deploy also shipped peer PRs #575, #578-#582, confirmed by Hein). 2026-09-30: Cause: withBusiestCompany opened plain BEGIN (READ COMMITTED), so a peer commit between two reads was seen by the later one only. Fix (#581, test-only): BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ; every read runs on the one ALS client in that snapshot. Deterministic regression test (a concurrent committed posted line mid-read) on a disposable fixture; plain BEGIN -> RED 3/3 ("expected 762 to be 760"), fix -> GREEN 10/10. The orchestrator verified isaflow_dev clean read-only (no R-165 journal, no orphan lines, no audit_log rows). Guard now a positive allowlist (localhost/127.0.0.1 AND database exactly isaflow_schema_fixture) in one function used by the skip and by both write helpers; cleanup verifies zero rows remain. Blind review r1 FIX (2 M, 4 L incl. the denylist letting isaflow_staging through), all fixed; r2 SHIP; master merges re-confirmed.

items.title: A payment link could be created for more than the invoice's outstanding balance, including on a fully paid invoice
items.sourceLabel: R-155 prod census and Hein's decision, 2026-09-30
items.claim: POST /api/portal/payment-link capped the amount only at the column maximum (R-158), so an owner/admin/manager could create a payable link for more than total_amount - amount_paid, or for any amount on a paid invoice.
items.severityRationale: Owner/admin/manager only (withCsrf + withWriteAccess). The link amount is what the pay page shows as Amount Due. The charge itself is computed at pay time by paystack/create (R-167) and is not changed here; on legacy negative or NaN amount_paid rows that charge can exceed the invoice total.
items.historicalDataImpact: Existing links are not changed. The R-155 prod census found 3 active links, all in ISAFlow Demo; one is on the fully paid INV-00553. It still displays, but paystack/create refuses to charge a paid invoice; Hein decided (2026-09-30) to leave it, so nothing was written on prod.
items.processNotes: 2026-09-30: Hein decided to cap a link at the outstanding balance (part payments allowed). Fixed: POST refuses an amount over total_amount - GREATEST(amount_paid, 0) (NULL or negative paid counts as 0), or any amount when that balance is NaN, with 400, compared in numeric, before any write. RED 4/4 on origin/master (R-166/red.int.log); mutants N1-N7 RED. Review round 1 (both reviewers FIX): NaN balance refused, negative amount_paid clamped to 0, deleted_at IS NULL added (pre-existing), R-158 max pinned by its message in k101, comment reason corrected, INV-00553 wording corrected. The adversarial MEDIUM (the link amount never controls the charge) is registered as R-167 for Hein. Mutants N1-N10 RED, N11 equivalent. Review round 2 (both reviewers: code ready, docs FIX): the 'cannot overcharge' claim corrected here, in fix.md and in R-167. /review (fresh blind agent): APPROVED, 4 LOW; fixed (no-balance message, stale test header, logs re-run on the head); drafts/pending_approval still get links (pre-existing, Hein's call). Mutants 13/14 RED, N11 equivalent. Merged as #576 (8209cfe3a). 2026-09-30: merged and deployed to prod ca5f32867 at 11:24 SAST on Hein's explicit business-hours 'Deploy now' (the deploy also shipped peer PRs #575, #578-#582, confirmed by Hein). Applied 0 migrations, golden paths 13/13, integrity green, RELEASE_SHA verified, fix strings in the live .next server chunks; health 200. Live: unauthenticated POST /api/portal/payment-link answers 401; 'the invoice has no outstanding balance' is in pages/api/portal/payment-link.js.

items.title: A portal payment link's amount is display-only: Paystack charges the invoice's full balance and no link is ever marked paid
items.claim: paystack/create reads only invoice_id, expires_at and status from portal_payment_links and charges Math.round((total - amount_paid) * 100) cents, the whole outstanding balance. The pay page shows the link's own amount as 'Amount Due'. So a part-payment link (e.g. R40.50 on a R115 invoice) shows R40.50 and charges R115. markPaymentLinkPaid has no caller, so a link stays 'active' after it is paid. The charge is also unclamped: a legacy row with a negative amount_paid is charged more than the invoice total (-50 on R115 charges R165); a NaN amount_paid yields NaN cents, and since NaN <= 0 is false the 'Invoice already paid' guard is skipped and NaN reaches initializeTransaction; and its invoice lookup has no company_id, status or deleted_at predicate, so an existing link on a since-cancelled or soft-deleted invoice is still chargeable.
items.severityRationale: The customer is shown one amount and charged another. On ordinary rows the charge is the outstanding balance; on legacy negative or NaN amount_paid rows it can exceed the invoice total or reach the gateway as NaN, and cancelled or soft-deleted invoices remain chargeable through an old link.
items.historicalDataImpact: Unknown. Prod census (read-only, for Hein): completed paystack_payment_requests with purpose 'customer_invoice' where amount_cents > 100 * total_amount of the invoice, or whose link amount differs from amount_cents; plus active links on invoices that are cancelled, soft-deleted, or have amount_paid < 0 or NaN.
items.processNotes: 2026-09-30: Found by the R-166 adversarial reviewer (reasoned from the code; confirmed by reading paystack/create.ts). Options for Hein: charge LEAST(link.amount, balance) in paystack/create (settlement already records amount_cents via recordGatewayInvoiceReceipt), and mark the link paid on completion; or show the balance on the pay page and drop part-payment links. Changes what customers are charged, so it needs Hein's decision. 2026-09-30: Hein decided: charge the link amount (LEAST of link amount and clamped balance), refuse NaN/cancelled/deleted, mark the link paid. Own PR. Fixed on the branch: resolveLinkCharge (min(link amount, total - GREATEST(amount_paid,0)) in numeric; NaN/cancelled/deleted/nothing owed refused before the gateway), migration 717 (paystack_payment_requests.portal_payment_link_id), settlement spends the link via recordGatewayInvoiceReceipt, the public GET offers only the chargeable amount. RED 11/13 on origin/master 66e776d81; GREEN 16/16; mutants 23/23 RED. Review round 1 (adversarial FIX, 2 MEDIUM + 4 LOW): Hein chose two kinds of link (the invoice's standing payment_url link charges the live balance and is never spent — portal_payment_links.charges_balance in 717, backfilled; explicit links charge their amount and are spent); create is transactional with the link locked and reuses a pending checkout for the same link and amount within 30 minutes; exact 'active' status; NaN link amount refused; GET says 'no outstanding balance'. Mutants 37/37 RED. Follow-ups noted: pay-now's own charge has no NaN/negative clamp; settlement never compares amount_cents to the event amount. Review round 2 (adversarial FIX, 1 HIGH introduced in round 1 + LOWs): create no longer holds a connection or the link lock across the Paystack call — a short locked transaction records the checkout (409 while starting), the gateway call runs outside it bounded at 10s, then the URL is stored or the checkout marked failed; rate-limited per IP and per link; charges_balance DEFAULT true replaces the payment_url backfill (mid-deploy and older standing links stay standing; only the POST writes false). Mutants 47/47 RED. Observed (pre-existing, all callers): checkRateLimit's LRU never writes its local counts, so one process admits several times the limit.
